text_chunks.title: What is a Track Hopper?
text_chunks.content: What is a Track Hopper? COAL WAGON bottom doors open ⬇⬇⬇ coal accumulating Track Hopper Pit (underground) Rail wagon with open bottom doors discharging coal by gravity into underground hopper A Track Hopper is an underground pit built beneath a rail track. Wagons with bottom-opening doors drive over it — coal falls straight through into the pit below. No tipping. No rotation. Just gravity.

text_chunks.title: Understanding Each Stage
text_chunks.content: Understanding Each Stage Stage | What Happens Here | Consequence if Disrupted ; Railway Wagon | Coal-loaded wagons arrive from the mine via rail. Each wagon carries 60–80 tonnes. | No coal input — entire downstream system starves. ; Wagon Tippler / Track Hopper | Wagon is inverted or coal falls through a grated pit. Coal drops into the hopper below. | Feed is interrupted — hopper level drops, feeder starves. ; Track Hopper / Surge Hopper | Acts as a buffer storage. Absorbs variation in wagon unloading rate. Feeds the conveyor steadily. | Overflow if feed is too fast; starvation if empty. ; Feeder / Crusher | Controls the rate at which coal is loaded onto the conveyor. May include a crusher to reduce lump size. | Overload or underload on conveyor; blockages if lumps are too large. ; Belt Conveyor BC-1 | Carries coal horizontally or at an incline to the transfer tower or directly to the bunker. | Entire downstream coal supply stops. ; Transfer Tower | Junction point where coal moves from one conveyor to another (BC-1 to BC-2). Contains a chute to guide coal. | Spillage, blockage, or coal misdirection. ; Coal Bunker | Large overhead storage silo (capacity 8–12 hours of operation). Continuously fed from conveyor above. | Bunker starves → boiler load reduction → unit outage. ; Boiler | Coal from bunker is pulverised and fired. Steam drives the turbine-generator. | Power generation stops. The belt conveyor is not an isolated machine . It is one critical link in a chain. An imbalance at any point — too much coal, too little coal, wrong size coal — travels downstream and amplifies. A senior engineer thinks of the entire chain simultaneously, not just the conveyor belt in front of them.

text_chunks.title: The Track Hopper Feeder — A Quick Refresh
text_chunks.content: The Track Hopper Feeder — A Quick Refresh You learned in L1 that coal discharged from the Wagon Tippler falls into the Underground Hopper. The Track Hopper Feeder is the device that meters coal from the bottom of that hopper onto the downstream belt conveyor at a controlled, steady rate. There are two main types you will encounter in Indian thermal power plants: WAGON tippled HOPPER FEEDER ★ THIS COURSE BELT CONVEYOR CRUSHER HOUSE COAL BUNKER / STOCK MILL → BOILER GENERATION POSITION OF FEEDER IN COAL FLOW CHAIN Every tonne through the boiler passes through this feeder first

text_chunks.title: System Flow Integration – End-to-End View
text_chunks.content: System Flow Integration – End-to-End View Wagon Tippler → Hopper → Feeder → Conveyor → Transfer Points → Coal Bunker → Boiler. The conveyor is not isolated — it is one link in a synchronised chain. Before you can understand the conveyor itself, you need to visualise the complete material flow — the journey coal takes from the moment it arrives at the plant to when it reaches the boiler. Think of it like a factory assembly line: every station depends on the one before it, and supplies the one after it. RAILWAY WAGON (Coal Source) Arrival point WAGON TIPPLER (Unloading) ~20–25 min/wagon TRACK HOPPER (Buffer) Coal storage pit FEEDER / CRUSHER (Sizing) Controls feed rate BELT CONVEYOR BC-1 (This Course) Primary conveying TRANSFER TOWER (High-risk zone) BC-1 → BC-2 COAL BUNKER (Final Buffer) Above the boiler BOILER (Combustion) ⚠ CRITICAL DELIVERY ZONE Transfer Tower + Bunker filling = high-risk area Coal Flow Direction → Each station is dependent on the previous — disruption at any point affects the entire chain
